title: Infinity-harmonic functions in the plane: Regularity by injectivity
summary: It has been a long standing conjecture that the $ \infty $-harmonic functions in the plane have a 1/3-Hölder continuous gradient. It \emph{is} known that solutions are $ C^1 $ and that the gradient is locally $ α$-Hölder, but $ α$ comes without any positive lower bound. Aronsson's solution $ x^{4/3} - y^{4/3} $ shows that no better general regularity is possible. In the plane there is also a connection between the $ \infty $-Laplace equation and the one-dimensional heat equation, observed already by Aronsson himself. I shall show that this link can be accessed under a certain injectivity…
